# Where Wsjr works now: the myths behind the markets

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Wsjr** works now.

The Osiris cycle is the best-preserved Egyptian myth, known from the Pyramid Texts onward: the good king murdered by his brother, the faithful wife who recovers him, the son who avenges him. It is simultaneously a story about kingship, about the flood that dies and returns, and about every human being who hoped to be judged worthy.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Wsjr
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Domain of influence:** Afterlife, Resurrection, Vegetation
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Energy & Natural World · Society & Spirit · Commerce & Governance
- **Strongest seat:** Agriculture, Food & Harvest
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 405 of 597

## The Myth at Work

**The Death of the Good King.** The earliest sources already presuppose the story: Osiris ruled as a beneficent king until his brother Seth, envious of his power, contrived his death — in the classical telling (Plutarch’s De Iside et Osiride, the fullest narrative we have) sealed in a chest and thrown into the Nile, the river carrying him to Byblos where a tamarisk grew to engulf the coffin. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.

**Isis the Faithful.** Isis searched for the body, recovered it from Byblos, and hid it — but Seth found it by night, cut it into fourteen pieces, and scattered them through Egypt.  Isis and Nephthys wandered the land gathering the fragments. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The green god of the Nile's return: his resurrection is the flood that fertilises the field — agriculture's founding myth.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Funerary & Memorial Services

*Funeral care, memorials, and legacy services. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The weighing of the heart and the first mummy are the canonical warrant for every funerary rite after them — Osiris IS the judged dead.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Wsjr performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### History, Archives & Records

*Museums, archives, libraries, and the record-keeping professions. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The Book of the Dead's judge — the archive of deeds, read aloud at the scales.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

*Law, courts, and regulatory compliance. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*The tribunal of the heart — the weighing against the feather is justice's oldest image.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

## The Long Employment

Osiris gave the West its archetype of the dying-and-rising god and Egyptology one of its oldest debates: Frazer’s “Osiris as vegetation deity” reading dominated a century before J.  Gwyn Griffiths and others restored his identity as dead king and judge. The age changed. The work did not.

## The Method, Stated Plainly

The atlas is not a horoscope. Seats are earned from the sources — argued, weighted, published — and every one of them can be challenged at the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). A match that cannot survive an argument does not survive review. That is the whole trick: the patterns are claims, and claims can be tested.

## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in agriculture, food & harvest, funerary & memorial services, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/osiris/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit.
